classification.difficultyReason: Requires an unprompted parallel construction to expose a right triangle, identify its perpendicular side as the difference of the radii, and apply Pythagoras.

content.prompt:
Two circles of radii $2\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$ have their centres $13\text{ cm}$ apart.

Find the length of the direct common tangent $PQ$.

spec.description: One wide figure containing two circles, their centre segment, both contact radii and the extended direct common tangent.
spec.mathematics: OC=13, OP=7 and CQ=2. The unit contact normal is (5/13,12/13), so the displayed line is tangent to both circles.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown x is retained; no right-angle squares or solution construction are added to the question.

answer.worked:
Draw $CH\parallel PQ$, meeting $OP$ at $H$. Radii are perpendicular to the tangent, so $HPQC$ is a rectangle: $PH=CQ=2\text{ cm}$ and $CH=PQ=x$.
$$\begin{align*}OH&=7-2=5\text{ cm}\\x^2+5^2&=13^2\\x^2&=144\\x&=12\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
